title: Kernel autoselect heuristics for H100/A100 (FP8/INT8) + guardrails + unit tests
author: Yuki Sato
commits: runtime/kernels: add KernelMode enum + per-GPU capability probe (SM90 vs SM80)
runtime/dispatch: implement AutoselectHeuristicsV2 for prefill/decode paths
runtime/dispatch: add shape regime bucketing (hidden_size/head_dim/seq_len) + telemetry tags
runtime/guardrails: enforce FP8 alignment constraints + fallback reasons surfaced to debug logs
runtime/config: add documented knobs + server-side override support

release_notes: Adds ADR-019 autoselect heuristics (behind flag) to choose FP8 vs INT8 vs baseline kernels on H100/A100 based on GPU arch + shape regime.
Adds explicit guardrails and fallback reason codes to reduce silent mis-dispatch under unsupported alignment/shape constraints.
Adds unit tests covering dispatch decisions for common hosted-model regimes (prefill/decode, short/medium/long context).
description:
Summary: Implements the ADR-019 kernel auto-selection heuristics for H100 (SM90) and A100 (SM80). The dispatcher now selects FP8 attention/matmul paths on H100 when shape + alignment constraints are satisfied and the workload is in a regime that consistently wins in our harness; otherwise it falls back to INT8 (A100-optimized) or baseline (FP16/BF16) kernels. This PR also adds unit tests for dispatch decisions and lightweight config docs so we can roll this out safely behind flags and per-model overrides.

Motivation: During the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint we saw that kernel-level wins did not translate uniformly end-to-end unless we were strict about shape regimes and correctness guardrails (alignment, head_dim, hidden_size multiples, seq_len buckets). We also need deterministic, reviewable selection logic to support perf canary gating and rapid rollback when regressions show up in a subset of prompts (e.g. TTFT spikes on short prompts in mixed prefill/decode traffic).

What changed (high level): 1) New AutoselectHeuristicsV2 entry point used by runtime dispatch for attention and GEMM-heavy blocks. 2) GPU capability probe: H100 (SM90) supports FP8 kernels; A100 (SM80) selects INT8 where supported, otherwise baseline. 3) Shape regime bucketing used by both attention and matmul dispatch: hidden_size bucketed by {<=4096, 4097-8192, >8192}; head_dim bucketed by {64, 128, other}; seq_len bucketed separately for prefill and decode (prefill: {<=512, 513-2048, >2048}; decode: {<=128, 129-512, >512}). 4) Guardrails + fallbacks: FP8 requires (a) head_dim in {64, 128}, (b) hidden_size % 128 == 0, (c) KV cache alignment constraints met, (d) kernel registry reports support for the exact (dtype/layout) tuple. If any guardrail fails we fall back to INT8 (if supported for that op on that GPU) else baseline. We also emit a structured fallback reason code (debug-only unless enabled) to support triage. 5) Config + docs: adds runtime flags for safe rollout: runtime.kernel_autoselect_v2_enabled (default false), runtime.kernel_autoselect_v2_allow_fp8 (default false), runtime.kernel_autoselect_v2_allow_int8 (default true), and per-model overrides via model registry / server-side config (documented in docs/internal/kernel-selection.md).

Heuristic specifics (matches ADR-019): H100: Prefer FP8 for decode-dominant traffic when decode seq_len <= 512 and head_dim in {64,128}; prefer FP8 for prefill when prefill seq_len in 513-2048 and batch_size >= 4 (continuous batching window makes this common) and hidden_size % 128 == 0; avoid FP8 for very short prefill (<=512) when concurrency is low (launch overhead dominates TTFT), and avoid FP8 for long-context prefill (>2048) unless explicitly forced by per-model override (we saw mixed results + higher variance). A100: Prefer INT8 matmul for supported shapes (alignment/packing constraints enforced by registry + guardrails); keep attention on baseline path unless INT8 attention is explicitly registered for the shape (not in this PR). If INT8 guardrails fail, fall back to baseline.

Testing: Adds golden tests that assert dispatch outcomes for a table of representative shapes (mapped to our “top hosted models” hidden sizes/head dims) across H100 and A100. Tests cover: FP8 selected when constraints are satisfied; INT8 selected on A100 when supported; fallback to baseline on unsupported head_dim / misalignment; stable bucketing across boundary values (e.g. seq_len 512/513, 2048/2049). Also adds a small test to ensure fallback reason codes are emitted and stable (string constants), so dashboards and triage tools don’t break.

Rollout plan: This is intended to ship disabled by default (flags off), then enabled in perf canary cohorts per model/region. Selection logic is deterministic and auditable, and it is safe to force baseline or disable FP8/INT8 per model if we see regressions (e.g. SUP-31844-style latency regression correlated with FP8 enablement in a region).

Notes/Follow-ups: - This PR intentionally does not change scheduler knobs; it assumes the instrumentation in pr-19855 and subsequent tuning PRs will be used to realize wins end-to-end. - We should wire the fallback reason codes into the new metric tagging (separate PR) once those tags exist. - Long-context FP8 quality caveats are handled by eval gating and per-model override policy (see ADR + quant profile policy).

Checklist: Added unit tests (dispatch + bucketing). Added internal docs with flag names and example overrides. Verified no behavior change when flags are off. Ran benchmark harness sanity locally on H100 (1 node) to confirm no unexpected dispatch flips when disabled.
review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka: Please make the FP8 guardrails explicit in code comments and ensure head_dim != 64/128 cannot silently pick FP8 even if registry has a kernel. Yuki Sato: Updated guardrails to hard-check head_dim set + added comment block referencing ADR-019 sections 3.1/3.2; added unit tests for head_dim=80 and 96. Noah Patel: I’m worried about the short-prefill TTFT regression we saw in the sprint. Can we default FP8 off even when autoselect_v2 is enabled, so we can stage INT8-only first? Yuki Sato: Added runtime.kernel_autoselect_v2_allow_fp8 (default false) separate from v2 enable; docs updated with suggested rollout order (baseline -> INT8 -> FP8). Rina Kobayashi: Tests should cover the seq_len boundary conditions (512/513, 2048/2049) and ensure bucketing doesn’t regress. Yuki Sato: Added boundary test cases + a bucketing golden file. Sofia Ivanova: Make sure selection for decode vs prefill is using the new scheduler-provided phase hint, not inferred from token counts (to avoid mixed-workload ambiguity). Yuki Sato: Updated call sites to plumb Phase::Prefill/Phase::Decode from scheduler instrumentation; added a small unit test to ensure phase hint is honored. Final: All reviewers approved after CI rerun (GPU smoke was flaky once; rerun passed).
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash; post-merge action item filed in ENG-7430 to enable in perf canary after thresholds land.
